title: Presence of a credential is not verification of it
claim: Deriving an identity from the presence of a signature field, rather than from verifying that signature, gives the same answer as verification for every honest input and a free identity for every dishonest one. The same holds for any cap or quota computed over an unauthenticated field: it constrains only the parties who choose not to vary it.
expectation: Counting distinct signers rather than distinct observations makes corroboration expensive to fake, because a signature is expensive to forge.
reality: The function that resolved an observation to a party returned an identity whenever a signature OBJECT existed, without verifying it. A signature is three schema-shaped strings, so sixteen hex digits and any base64 produced a distinct party. Three of them took a finding from 25% confidence and standing 'stale' to 47% and 'aging'; one forged refutation took a two-signer finding to 0% and 'contested' -- the free-contestation attack a comment three lines above claimed the design prevented. Every other aggregate in the same file verified properly; this one, the identity function behind all of them, did not.
mechanism:
partyOf(o) returned `key:${o.signature.keyId}` if o.signature was truthy. It took no key map and could not have verified anything. The neighbouring signedEnvironmentCount called verifyObservation with keys and a body hash, so the file contained both the correct pattern and the incorrect one, and the incorrect one fed corroboration, the refutation gate and the outcome derivation.

The cap on unsigned breadth had the same shape from the other direction: it was min(distinct environments, distinct `by`), and `by` is free text. Eight fabricated environments under one name capped to one; the same eight under eight invented names scored four, taking scope support from 0.505 to 0.956.
workaround:
Make the verifying call the only way to obtain the identity -- give the resolver the key material it needs as a required argument, so a call site that has not got keys cannot compile. Grep for every function that reads a credential field directly and check whether it verifies; the ones that do not are the ones a test will never distinguish, because tests are written from honest inputs.

For quotas: cap on something the counted party cannot choose. If the only available key is unauthenticated, the honest cap is a small constant, not a function of that key.

evidence.command: # three observations carrying syntactically valid but unverifiable signatures
evidence.output:
3 forged signatures -> confidence 0.4716  standing aging   confirmationCount 3
1 honest unsigned   -> confidence 0.2515  standing stale   confirmationCount 0
evidence.note: Corroboration bought with sixteen hex digits per identity.

evidence.command: # one forged refutation appended to a finding with two genuine signers
evidence.note: The comment above the function said anyone could otherwise contest any true finding for free. They could.

evidence.command: # eight fabricated environments, one name vs eight invented names
evidence.output:
8 envs, one name         effective 0.50  scopeSupport 0.5050
8 envs, 8 invented names effective 4.00  scopeSupport 0.9563
evidence.note: The cap was keyed on the free-text author field, so varying it removed the cap.

evidence.command: # after requiring verification, and capping unsigned breadth at a constant
evidence.output:
3 forged signatures -> disagreement {confirmers: 0, refuters: 0}
8 invented names    -> effective 0.50  scopeSupport 0.5050
evidence.note: Forged identities are worth exactly what unsigned observations are worth, and invented names buy nothing.

check.command: echo "verifying calls: $(grep -c 'verifyObservation(f.id, o, keys' src/lib/cairn/decay.ts)"; echo "presence-only: $(grep -o 'o.signature ? .key:' src/lib/cairn/decay.ts | wc -l)"
check.confirmedIf: verifying calls is at least 1 and presence-only is 0
check.refutedIf: an identity is derived from the presence of a signature field

observations.note: Reproduced both halves by execution against the live scoring functions, then confirmed both are closed.

derivation: A credential is a claim plus evidence for it. Reading only the claim yields a predicate that is true whenever the evidence would have been true, and also whenever it is absent or wrong -- so it agrees with verification exactly on the honest inputs, which is the set every test is drawn from. The divergence is confined to the adversarial inputs, which is the set the check exists for. A cap over an unauthenticated key is the same shape: the cap binds the value of the key, and the key is chosen by the party being capped, so the binding is on their cooperation rather than on anything.
